title: Patch kernel-scheduler regression causing token throughput drop for medium-context models
creator: Samir Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sudden TTFT regressions and sustained tokens/sec drops starting 2026-03-11 across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Regression surfaced after rolling runtime-1.19 to a subset of fleets. Affected workloads: medium-context generation (<=1024 tokens) and models with longer KV lifetimes (eg. redwood-14b-v1, community-7b variants). Symptoms: 20-40% tokens/sec reduction in steady-state, 30-80ms TTFT increase on short requests, and increased request queueing on Dedicated pools under burst load. This ticket captures triage, short-term mitigations, root-cause investigation, and the urgent patch delivery plan.
acceptance_criteria: Restore tokens/sec to within 5% of pre-1.19 baseline across representative workloads
TTFT regression for 1-32 token prompts reduced to <15ms delta versus baseline
Hotfix validated on Hosted canary, Dedicated reserved pool, and sample Private deploy (customer sandbox)
Customer-facing incident postmortem published and affected customers notified with remediation timeline
steps_taken: 2026-03-11 22:15 UTC: On-call alerted via PagerDuty after Pager rule triggered for increased tail latency on hosted-production cluster eu-west-1
Immediate telemetry inspection: spike in runqueue wait time and per-GPU kernel launch variance correlated with runtime-1.19 rollout window
Reproduced tokens/sec drop using benchmark harness (workload-profile A,B,C) on a local mirror of dedicated pool: confirmed ~32% reduction for redwood-14b-v1 at seq=512
Scoped commits between runtime-1.18 -> 1.19: identified kernel-scheduler heuristic change commit 'scheduler: adaptive-stride v2' as first suspect (commit 3a7f2b6)
Created guarded canary: pinned a small set of hosted nodes to runtime-1.18 which restored baseline throughput for the same requests
Opened rollback window and coordinated with infra to limit additional 1.19 rotations until hotfix validated
root_cause_summary: An optimization in kernel-scheduler intended to improve throughput for long sequences changed stride calculation that reduced aggregation opportunities for medium-length KV caches. The heuristic favored larger stride bundling which increased per-kernel latency for short, frequent inference calls and reduced effective token throughput under our continuous-batching pattern. The change interacted poorly with the runtime's batching boundary detection when KV reuse lifetime < 2k tokens, causing increased kernel-launch overhead and more frequent kernel churn.
mitigations: Hotpatch: revert adaptive-stride v2 heuristic and restore previous stride calculation (PR #4112)
Temporary routing: re-route high-ttft customer traffic to nodes pinned to runtime-1.18 for Hosted and provide guidance for Dedicated customers to redeploy with runtime-1.18 manifest
Autoscaling tweak: raised per-GPU request queue cap to reduce queueing during rollback to avoid customer throttles
Private customers: inboxed customized upgrade rollback instructions and offered remote assist for sandbox validation
patch_plan: Draft fix: refine stride heuristic to consider KV-lifetime histogram and batch size distribution (branch fix/kern-sched-25714)
Bench: run 48-hr regression matrix (seq 16/64/256/512/1024) across redwood-14b-v1, redwood-7b-q4_0, and open-llama-7b; measure TTFT and tokens/sec
Canary rollout: staged canary to 5% hosted nodes -> 25% -> 100% if metrics stable; Dedicated hotfix image available for reserve pools
PRs: code change PR #4120, rollback PR #4112 (guarded), runtime package build #789, and merge gating by Lina and infra lead
Customer validation: test checklist for affected customers and dedicated pool owners
